name: Laugavegur Trail
summary: A 55 km hut-to-hut route across the southern highlands from the hot springs at Landmannalaugar to the birch woods of Þórsmörk, by way of the rhyolite hills and snowfields at Hrafntinnusker, Álftavatn and the black sands of Emstrur. Several rivers are unbridged and have to be waded.

name: Fimmvörðuháls Trek
summary: A 22–25 km crossing from Skógar to Þórsmörk over the pass between the Eyjafjallajökull and Mýrdalsjökull ice caps, climbing beside the waterfalls of the Skógá and passing the craters Magni and Móði left by the 2010 eruption. Most people walk it in one long day; two huts on the pass allow it to be split.

name: Laugavegur & Fimmvörðuháls Trek
summary: The Laugavegur walked end to end and then continued over the Fimmvörðuháls pass to Skógar, making one continuous line from Landmannalaugar to the south coast. It is normally sold as a six-day hut-to-hut itinerary.

name: Hornstrandir Trek
summary: Walking in the uninhabited Hornstrandir reserve in the northern Westfjords, reached by boat from Ísafjörður or Bolungarvík and put together from fjord-to-fjord stages over passes such as Hafnarskarð and Kjaransvíkurskarð. There is no single fixed route, no road access and no resupply; paths are largely unmarked and several rivers are unbridged.

name: Kjalvegur Trail
summary: The old Kjölur horse route through the central highlands between Hveravellir and Hvítárnes, on the corridor between the Langjökull and Hofsjökull ice caps, with huts at Þjófadalir, Þverbrekknamúli and Hvítárnes. The ground stays high and fairly level throughout and the line is marked by cairns and posts.
